weekend_note: Isaias has moved inland and the weather is calm: sunny and warm today near the mid 80s, with little rain in the forecast this week. The bigger issue is recovery, since Escambia County had about 127,000 customers without power on Saturday morning and a systemwide precautionary boil-water notice from ECUA. City event permits were canceled through today, so treat outdoor and beach events as unconfirmed until organizers say otherwise. Picks for the coming days are the Blue Angels practice on Oct 14, Beach-O-Ween and Gallery Night on Oct 16, Ice Flyers on Oct 17 (indoors at the Bay Center) and Barktoberfest on Oct 18.

news.title: Isaias hits the Panhandle, Escambia hardest for outages
news.summary: The storm came ashore near Destin late Friday as a Category 2 with 105 mph winds and weakened over Alabama, and the Hurricane Center ended advisories early Saturday. About 127,000 customers in Escambia County were without power, roughly 73 percent of those tracked, the most of any Florida county.

news.title: ECUA issues systemwide boil-water notice
news.summary: Emerald Coast Utilities Authority put a precautionary boil-water notice in place across its Escambia County system while crews check wells and other infrastructure. The report did not say when it will be lifted, so watch ECUA for updates.

news.title: Milton assesses heavy wind damage
news.summary: WEAR reports winds above 100 mph in Milton, leaving streets littered with downed trees, debris and loose power lines. Some displaced families went to the community center, and Santa Rosa County set a dusk-to-dawn curfew for Saturday night. A headline on the page also notes two deaths in Escambia County.

news.title: Calmer weather ahead, but river flooding is a concern
news.summary: FOX10 expects sun and highs near 80 on Sunday and says rivers can keep rising after the rain stops. A flood warning was in effect, and officials asked people to avoid unnecessary travel and follow curfews. Another FOX10 headline says rain chances stay near zero much of this week.

news.title: Festa Italiana moves to mid-November
news.summary: The downtown festival planned for Oct 9 and 10 is now set for Nov 13 and 14 from 11 AM to 6 PM at Fountain Park. Admission stays free, and organizers cited safety for volunteers, vendors and guests.

news.title: City and county closures covered the storm weekend
news.summary: County offices were closed Thursday afternoon and Friday, and the City of Pensacola canceled rentals and event permits through Sunday, Oct 11. Pensacola State College closed Friday and Saturday, and UWF suspended classes starting Thursday. No reopening dates had been posted in that report.

coverage_note: Written around 3 AM Sunday Oct 11, the day after Isaias, and most reporting found was from Saturday morning, so power, water, beach and event status may already have changed; confirm anything outdoors or on the beach with the organizer. The forecast comes from a WEAR page that showed weekday names without dates (read as Oct 11 to 15); FOX10 describes lower rain chances, and no forecast past Oct 15 was found. Must Do Pensacola, Local Pulse, the City of Pensacola news page, the Saenger and Ice Flyers sites, and NorthEscambia.com would not load or could not be searched usefully, so the weekly events list, Saenger shows, Ice Flyers and Blue Wahoos entries are carried over from earlier checks. Three events were added from Visit Pensacola's fall list (dates only). No post-storm word was found from organizers, and Gonzalez and north Escambia coverage remains thin, limited to county library classes already listed. Restaurant statuses are unchanged; Pelican Bar and Grill and Casa Luvia remain unconfirmed, and no new openings or closings were found this run. The Oct 17 Ali Siddiq show at the Saenger could not be rechecked.
